projectDescription: A placement-portfolio web application that recommends tourist destinations from a curated dataset using explainable, preference-based scoring. The MVP will collect trip preferences such as interests, budget, duration, and season, then rank destinations and explain each match. The plan should emphasize resume-ready engineering outcomes and practical future AI enhancements.

questions.question: Which language should the Tourist Recommendation Web App use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing and supports maintainable, placement-ready frontend code.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: A familiar option for a straightforward web frontend.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is a strong default for a portfolio project because it demonstrates type-safe frontend development.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should the Tourist Recommendation Web App use?

options.label: React
options.description: A widely used component-based framework with a large ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive framework suitable for an approachable interactive app.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with an opinionated application structure.

questions.rationale: React and TypeScript are widely recognized skills for entry-level software roles.

questions.question: What should the Tourist Recommendation Web App include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive destination discovery, preference form (interests, budget, trip duration, and season), ranked recommendation cards with match explanations, destination detail views, and a polished demo/portfolio presentation.
questions.answer: Responsive destination discovery, preference form (interests, budget, trip duration, and season), ranked recommendation cards with match explanations, destination detail views, and a polished demo/portfolio presentation.
questions.rationale: These features make the recommendation flow easy to demonstrate and explain in a placement interview.

questions.question: Which language should the Recommendation API use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Shares typed models across the API and frontend and supports a consistent JavaScript stack.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses the Node.js ecosystem without static typing.

options.label: Python
options.description: A common language for data processing and machine-learning experiments.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: A strongly typed option with mature web API tooling.

questions.rationale: TypeScript supports a single, approachable stack while leaving a clear path to more advanced recommendation models.

questions.question: Which framework should power the Recommendation API?

options.label: Azure Functions
options.description: A serverless option for event-driven or HTTP-triggered APIs.

questions.rationale: Express is a simple custom API framework that fits the proposed Node.js and TypeScript MVP.

questions.question: What should the Recommendation API include?
questions.recommendedChoice: REST endpoints for destinations and recommendations; an explainable weighted content-based ranking algorithm using trip preferences; validation, error handling, and PostgreSQL persistence; and a small curated destination dataset suitable for a live demo.
questions.answer: REST endpoints for destinations and recommendations; an explainable weighted content-based ranking algorithm using trip preferences; validation, error handling, and PostgreSQL persistence; and a small curated destination dataset suitable for a live demo.
questions.rationale: An explainable ranking MVP is achievable without relying on paid AI APIs or claiming a trained model where no feedback data exists.

questions.question: Which data stores does the project need?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Stores structured destination data and supports future user feedback and saved recommendations.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Stores uploaded files or media assets.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only when the application does not need persistence, file/object storage, queues, caches, or an associated storage account.

questions.rationale: PostgreSQL is appropriate for structured destinations and leaves room to add feedback-based personalization later.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application API features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users need accounts to access application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: The MVP is publicly usable without sign-in.

questions.rationale: Sign-in is not necessary for the first portfolio demo and can be added if personalized accounts are introduced later.
